newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Union plays down KLM alliance talk.
newsitem.headline: Union plays down KLM alliance talk.

text.p: Dutch flag carrier KLM and its flight attendants' union on Wednesday played down a fresh spate of alliance rumours which powered the stock higher on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange.

KLM was one of the morning's highest climbers, gaining 1.40 guilders or 3.25 percent to 44.70 after financial daily Het Financieele Dagblad reported Dutch and Swiss unions were meeting in Zurich to discuss a possible KLM-Swissair link-up.
"The report comes as a complete surprise to me," KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuner said.
Cabin crew union VNC confirmed it was meeting Swiss counterpart Capers for talks on the consequences of a possible Swissair-KLM link-up, but stressed they were routine.
"Talks like these are routine union business," spokesman Henri Popelier said. "We have had no indications that KLM is gearing up a partnership with Swissair, we've heard nothing."
He said VNC had recently held similar discussions with Iberia unions.
"KLM said itself it is seeking a strong European partner," Popelier said. "Based on that we maintain contacts with unions connected to the likely candidates."
These included Swissair, Iberia and possibly Alitalia, Popelier said.
A spokesman for Swissair told Reuters on Wednesday that "an alliance with KLM is not an issue at Swissair right now".

KLM's Wellhuner also said the Dutch carrier had no comment to make on speculation it was poised to link up with Iberia after Spain's industry minister said on Tuesday it expected the Spanish carrier to forge a foreign alliance before the year-end.
Industry minister Josep Pique said Iberia was conducting "intense negotiations" with foreign companies such as KLM and British Airways Plc.
"In this sector everyone is always talking to everyone," KLM's Wellhuner said, adding KLM was prepared to comment only when such talks had a reasonable likelihood of yielding something substantive.
"At present we have nothing to say," he said.
